sentences.text: Leanne Marsh is the person being assessed.
The assessment is Leanne's review.
The person is currently living with her mother.
The person's mother has bad knees.
Leanne helps her mother with hoovering.
Leanne enjoys art and is working on a large painting of her cat Biscuit.
Leanne enjoys cooking on Mondays.
Leanne enjoys the disco on Fridays.
Leanne currently travels to the service via minibus.
Leanne likes the idea of the practice bus trips.
The social worker will bring Leanne a simple, easy-read document about what happens next.
Leanne does not like Dave, the driver of the minibus.
Dave touches Leanne on her chest on the minibus.
Dave touches Leanne between her legs over her trousers on the minibus.
Dave kisses Leanne on her mouth.
Dave says it is a 'secret' between them and does not want Leanne to tell her mother.
These incidents occur every week when Leanne is the last person to get off the minibus.
The incidents started after Leanne's birthday in August.
Leanne denies that the incidents were stories and confirms they are true.
No staff at Brookside have touched Leanne in a similar way.
The social worker will inform the safeguarding team at the council and the police about the incidents.
The social worker will ensure Leanne is accompanied if police or safeguarding staff speak to her.
Leanne is not in trouble for what happened.
Leanne is not at risk of harm from staff at Brookside.
Leanne will not be travelling on Dave's minibus from tomorrow.
Leanne requests a taxi instead of her mother driving.
The social worker will contact the centre manager Joanne to arrange a taxi from Wednesday onwards.
The social worker will visit Leanne's house tomorrow at 4 o'clock to inform her mother together.
Leanne would like Biscuit (her cat) to be present at the meeting with her mother.
The social worker will ask Sue to arrange two practice bus trips into town in December as part of travel training.
